function.uniprot_function: Histone acetyltransferase (HAT) that functions as transcriptional coactivator regulating gene expression via chromatin remodeling. Acetylates all four core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) in nucleosomes. Also acetylates non-histone proteins including transcription factors (TP53, E2F1, GATA1, MYB, CTNNB1, HIF1A, NFκB), affecting protein-DNA interactions, protein stability, and transcriptional activity. Mediates cAMP-gene regulation by binding phosphorylated CREB. Recruited to chromatin by transcription factors to activate gene expression. Has intrinsic polyubiquitin ligase activity (E3/E4) for p53 in cytoplasm. Involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, DNA repair, and development. Auto-acetylates to regulate own activity.
function.catalytic_activity: Acetyl-CoA + [histone]-L-lysine = CoA + [histone]-N6-acetyl-L-lysine; transfers acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to epsilon-amino group of lysine residues
function.tissue_specificity: Ubiquitously expressed across human tissues with particularly high levels in bone marrow. Expression varies across tissues and developmental stages.

biological_process.term: regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

reactome.pathway_name: TCF dependent signaling in response to WNT
TP53 Regulates Transcription of DNA Repair Genes

pathways.pathway_role_summary: EP300 is a central transcriptional coactivator involved in 141+ Reactome pathways. Key roles include: (1) Wnt/beta-catenin signaling as histone acetyltransferase at TCF target genes (differentiation vs CBP for proliferation), (2) p53 pathway as acetylase activating p53 transcriptional function and stability, (3) Hypoxia response via HIF1A acetylation and coactivation, (4) Notch signaling, (5) TGF-beta/SMAD signaling, (6) JAK-STAT signaling, (7) CREB/cAMP signaling, (8) Nuclear receptor signaling (ERα, PPARγ), (9) Cell cycle regulation via E2F1/RB1, (10) Development (HOX genes, heart, lung, cartilage). Acts as integrator of multiple signal-dependent transcription events.

disease_associations.description: Autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in EP300 (8-10% of RSTS cases). Characterized by intellectual disability, distinctive craniofacial features, broad thumbs/halluces, postnatal growth retardation, and joint hyperlaxity. Incidence 1:100,000-1:125,000 live births. Mutations include frameshift, nonsense, splice site, missense, and large deletions. Most are de novo; mosaic mutations described.

EP300 mutations found in various cancers including colorectal, gastric, breast, hepatocellular carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, and hematological malignancies. Mutations correlate with genome instability, altered DNA damage repair pathways, and poor prognosis. Pathways enriched in EP300-mutated cancers: cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, cell cycle, p53 signaling, JAK-STAT signaling. EP300 promotes cancer cell proliferation via Hippo-YAP and other oncogenic pathways.

metadata.data_quality_notes: High-quality data from multiple authoritative sources. Canonical sequence not directly extracted (UniProt web interface requires JavaScript). Domain boundaries vary slightly between sources (±5-20 residues is normal). PTM data comprehensive from PhosphoSitePlus/iPTMnet. Kinetic data limited: only MYB KIX binding (Kd 3.8 μM) quantified; most other interactions lack kinetic parameters. ~400+ protein interactions reported in literature; top 20 high-confidence partners included here. EP300 contains extensive intrinsically disordered regions between structured domains.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: EP300 is a critical hub protein in cell signaling as a transcriptional coactivator integrating multiple pathways (Wnt, p53, hypoxia, TGF-beta, JAK-STAT, CREB, nuclear receptors). Key modeling considerations: (1) Acetylates both histones and transcription factors, affecting gene expression globally. (2) Nucleocytoplasmic shuttling regulated by AMPK (S89 phosphorylation) controls mTORC1 activity. (3) Auto-acetylation at K1499/K1549/K1554/K1560 positively regulates activity. (4) Competes with HDAC1/2 for chromatin binding; acetylates HDAC1 to inhibit it. (5) Multiple interaction domains (TAZ1, KIX, TAZ2, IBiD, bromodomain) enable combinatorial binding to diverse transcription factors. (6) Differential roles vs paralog CREBBP in Wnt signaling (p300=differentiation, CBP=proliferation). (7) Has E3/E4 ubiquitin ligase activity for cytoplasmic p53. (8) Limited quantitative kinetic data available; most interactions qualitative. Mutations cause Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome and drive multiple cancers.
